open_points.subject: white-space policy constant
open_points.text: The set is one value of the release; its home in the code, the data provider's constant the reading code imports (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1), is State 6's to give.
open_points.question: What imported data-provider symbol will carry the fixed white-space set to generated code?
options: Declare a dedicated constant such as UNICODE_WHITE_SPACE_CODE_POINTS.
Declare a validation-policy constant scoped to blank-value checking.
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated immutable UNICODE_WHITE_SPACE_CODE_POINTS constant.
consequences: A general Unicode-named constant can be reused consistently wherever the specification reads white space.
A validation-scoped constant narrows its apparent use but risks another module independently defining the same set.
open_points.requirement: White space, here and wherever this specification reads a given value's white space, is exactly the 25 code points of Unicode's `White_Space` property: U+0009 to U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000; no other character is white space, whatever a language's own operation counts, and `strip(v)` below removes these from both ends of `v`.

open_points.subject: test release for disclosure-class enforcement
open_points.text: The check is made on every answer all the same, and it is shown on a test release whose class tables — the imported `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES` constant and the imported `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS` constant (SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1) — differ from the first release's in the one row a test gives (Required tests 5 and 6).
open_points.question: How will the Factory construct the alternate release, and which concrete service, answer and field will its changed row use?
options: Generate a complete alternate data-provider fixture containing the changed constants.
Inject alternate constant tables into a test build while leaving production constants untouched.
open_points.default_guess: Generate a complete alternate release fixture and use one Kernel-reachable answer with one added personal-data field.
consequences: A complete fixture tests the real release path but adds fixture-generation work.
Injection is smaller but can bypass errors in release assembly or imports.
open_points.requirement: An answer that would carry a class above the token's highest is refused whole; Registry never answers part of it.

open_points.subject: owner-interface host isolation
open_points.text: The host name is a fact of the deployment, which Registry cannot check, as the addresses are (A17 rule 1): providing it and keeping every other HTTPS service of the host off it is a deployment step, carried to the deployment's owner (the Factory's platform deployment).
open_points.question: Which host name, DNS or hosts-file mapping, TLS endpoint and service-routing arrangement will provide the isolated owner-interface host?
options: Use a dedicated VPN-resolved DNS name terminating TLS directly at Registry.
Use a dedicated VPN-resolved DNS name at a reverse proxy that routes only that name to Registry.
Use a dedicated hosts-file name with a locally managed certificate and no other HTTPS virtual host.
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated VPN-only DNS name at a reverse proxy with no other route for that host name.
consequences: Direct TLS minimizes intermediaries but requires Registry to own certificate handling.
A reverse proxy centralizes TLS but must be checked not to expose another service under the same host name.
A hosts-file name avoids DNS infrastructure but increases per-client administration.
open_points.requirement: the deployment gives the owner interface a host name of its own, under which no other HTTPS service answers — on the home server not the kernel workplace, the gateway or PresuPro — and no other service of the same host receives the owner session cookie.

open_points.subject: confirmation-time id-collision verification
open_points.text: Through Registry's surfaces alone a minted id cannot be chosen, so the refusal is checked on the code by the Factory — `confirm_import` builds the mapping inside the confirming transaction and applies it only when clean — and carried to Factory verification (2026-11-25, round-120 T1).
open_points.question: How will the Factory deterministically create the post-step collision and verify the transactional clean-mapping guard without making an accidental hidden function shape part of the contract?
options: Inject a deterministic random source so a normal create mints a picked id, then exercise confirmation through its public surface.
Use a controlled store fixture to insert the colliding record after the step, then exercise confirmation through its public surface.
Use a structural check tied to an exact `confirm_import` implementation symbol and its transaction body.
open_points.default_guess: Inject the random source and verify the refusal, unchanged store and refreshed conflicting mapping through public behavior; use structural checking only for the otherwise unobservable transaction boundary.
consequences: Random-source injection follows the admitted history but requires a replaceable randomness dependency.
A store fixture is simpler but creates state no Registry operation produced.
An exact-symbol structural check is brittle and improperly couples verification to hidden implementation names.
open_points.requirement: A confirmation applies the mapping of the file and the picks it is bound to (rule 2, A13 rule 6), which it builds once, from the kept bytes, inside the confirming transaction, as it must to write the records; it applies that mapping only when it is clean, and otherwise refuses the whole import, and nothing changes (R0-50, R0-79).

open_points.subject: snapshot instant verification
open_points.text: The tests' clocks do not move between two reads of one run, so an implementation taking a backup's instant later than the read that fixes its snapshot (rule 1) is not told apart; that remains carried to Factory verification.
open_points.question: How will Factory verification prove that the recorded instant is read at the first snapshot-fixing read rather than at a later point in the run?
options: Use an instrumented clock whose value changes immediately after the audit-sequence read that fixes the snapshot.
Use an instrumented store backend that records event order and assert the clock read occurs at the snapshot-fixing read.
Use a structural check of the backup transaction's ordering.
open_points.default_guess: Use instrumented clock and store ports to assert both the recorded value and event order.
consequences: Instrumented ports give deterministic behavioral evidence but require suitable seams in later contracts.
A store event trace is precise but couples the check to backend instrumentation.
A structural check is simpler but more sensitive to harmless implementation refactoring.
open_points.requirement: The copy's read transaction fixes its snapshot by its first read, which is of the audit counter's last sequence number, and the instant is read from the clock at that read;

set_aside.subject: A02-1 and A02-2 Required tests
set_aside.text: A project with a display name of three spaces is refused.
set_aside.question: Which Required test must show that all 25 listed code points, including non-ASCII ones, are treated as white space, that no other code point is, and that the rule applies to both required and optional values?
options: Add a parameterized test covering every listed code point, representative combinations, and a nearby excluded code point for required and optional values.
Name a smaller set of boundary representatives that the required test must exercise and carry exhaustive checking to factory_checks.
set_aside.default_guess: Require exhaustive parameterized coverage of the closed 25-code-point set plus at least one excluded character.
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: failed removal of a newly made store
set_aside.text: A removal that fails, leaving an empty store of the release's version, cannot be made to happen through the surfaces without failing the store's making too; it is carried to Factory verification.
set_aside.question: How will the Factory distinguish and force failure of the cleanup removal after successful store creation without also preventing that creation?
options: Inject filesystem operations and fail only the cleanup removal call.
Run against a purpose-built filesystem fault harness that changes permissions after creation.
Use a structural check of the listener-failure cleanup branch.
set_aside.default_guess: Inject filesystem operations and fail only the precisely identified cleanup removal.
consequences: Operation injection is deterministic but requires a filesystem boundary in the generated design.
A filesystem harness is closer to deployment behavior but may be platform-sensitive.
A structural check avoids platform faults but gives weaker evidence of the resulting store contents.
set_aside.requirement: a start whose listener cannot be opened => it serves nothing, leaves no listener of it open, and the store holds the records it held before that start — for a store that start made new, no store, or, when its removal fails, an empty one holding no record but its audit sequence at 0   -- A17-4
